domains.name: Artificial Intelligence
domains.description: Methods for building systems that learn, reason, generate, retrieve, and act under uncertainty.

edges.rationale: The paradigms differ primarily in whether task labels define the learning signal.
Supervised examples are usually exogenous, while an RL policy changes its future observations.
Expected loss and probabilistic prediction require conditional probability reasoning.
Empirical risk minimization is a core supervised-learning formulation.
Generalization analysis starts by distinguishing empirical from population risk.
A valid holdout design is needed to estimate deployment performance.
Leakage is diagnosed relative to split boundaries, prediction time, and unit of independence.
Leaked evaluation is not evidence of generalization.
Regularization is best understood as trading approximation bias for reduced estimation variance.
Bias and variance explain why low training error need not transfer.
Linear predictors are a foundational supervised model class.
Coordinate-wise penalties have meaning only relative to feature units.
Feature scales strongly affect curvature and optimization conditioning.
Most neural networks are fitted with gradient-based optimization.
Backpropagation questions assume an understanding of composed neural transformations.
Gradient flow determines which learned representations receive task signal.
Attention operates on and constructs learned representations.
Attention is the central token-mixing component of a transformer.
Calibration is a conditional-frequency property of probabilistic forecasts.
A score can order cases well while its numeric probabilities remain unreliable.
Cost-derived probability thresholds require trustworthy probability semantics.
Optimal action thresholds follow from comparing conditional expected costs.
Prevalence changes how ranking metrics, especially precision-recall summaries, should be interpreted.
Shift analysis refines what future distribution a generalization claim covers.
Shift types are distinguished through different factorizations of joint distributions.
Predictive association alone does not identify an intervention effect.
Joint and latent-variable models require probability factorization.
The primary contrast is joint or data-process modeling versus direct conditional prediction.
Discriminative prediction is a major supervised-learning approach.
Methods such as PCA learn structure without labels.
Clustering is a canonical unsupervised task.
Variance-based projections depend on the units of their coordinates.
Distance-based clusters depend on feature scale and geometry.
Bellman reasoning formalizes the sequential objective in reinforcement learning.
Off-policy evaluation assumes policies, trajectories, returns, and behavior data.
Importance ratios and support conditions are probabilistic concepts.
Knowledge tracing updates uncertain latent skill state from noisy observations.
A learner model should not interpret response likelihoods more literally than their calibration supports.
Expected information gain is one principled question-selection objective.
Adaptive selection consumes and updates the learner state maintained by knowledge tracing.
An adaptive policy must remain valid for new learners and avoid overfitting item history.
Autoregressive likelihood is a product of conditional token probabilities.
Autoregressive language modeling is a sequence-specific generative factorization.
Scaling is understood relative to query-key dot products and softmax attention.
The autoregressive factorization determines which sequence positions are future information.
Causal masking is implemented inside transformer attention blocks.
Retrieved passages condition a generator whose sequence behavior must still be evaluated.
Grounding cannot exceed the relevance and authority of the available retrieved evidence.
Tool calls begin as model outputs but require a separate execution boundary.
An observation loop distinguishes proposed calls from executed actions and returned state.
Retrieval is one tool-mediated way an agent can acquire external evidence.

objective_edges.rationale: Order-behavior predictions require tracing what content-only attention routes before deciding what changes without a positional signal.
Resource scaling follows from identifying the pairwise score and weighted-value intermediates created by attention.
Distinguishing Transformer information paths requires knowing how an attention sublayer moves source values between positions.
Reasoning about non-commuting sublayer composition first requires distinguishing the information path implemented by each sublayer.
Causal visibility constrains the same query-key comparisons and value routes that unmasked attention would otherwise permit.
Predicting logit scaling effects requires locating query-key scores before softmax and separating them from routed values.
Tracing an incremental cache requires knowing which prior positions a newly generated token may attend to under causal visibility.
Distinguishing cached from recomputed tensors requires tracing information through attention and the surrounding Transformer sublayers.
Reconciling an agent's external state requires first distinguishing a model proposal from an authorized, executed tool action whose observation can change that state.

sources.title: AI foundations bundle schema conventions
sources.locator: Local schema version 1.0.0
sources.notes: Edges point from a prerequisite, component, or contrasted concept to the downstream or paired concept. Question difficulty is an expert-prior IRT b value; discrimination is an expert-prior IRT a value; guess_rate and slip_rate are probabilities. Concept weights sum to 1. Correct options have a null misconception_id; every distractor names exactly one misconception. These priors require empirical recalibration.
